uncited: This method completes the Exact Visibility Ordering for Cell Projection Volume Rendering (SXMPVO) algorithm by generating a global topological sort of mesh cells.

It extends the standard MPVO Phase II by incorporating Pseudo-Neighbor (PN) relations derived from image-space occlusion, ensuring a correct segment sorting order for volume rendering on unstructured meshes.
It differs from its sibling [BSP-XMPVO](1160-bsp-xmpvo.md) by using image-space scan conversion to determine occlusion rather than spatial partitioning.
The method operates on the data structures and intermediate results (PIX lists) produced by the SXMPVO Phase I (scan conversion).
- For each cell, a `sink_cell_flag` (boolean).
- For each cell, a `PN_list` (linked list of PN entries).
- A total ordering of all cells in the mesh, suitable for front-to-back or back-to-front volume rendering.
- **PN Entry**: Contains `occluded_cell_number` (integer) and `next` (pointer).
- **PIX List**: A singly linked list of PIX entries, sorted by decreasing `z`.
Iterate through every PIX list in the A-Buffer.
Discard the first entry (back-facing face where ray exits mesh) and the last entry (back-facing face where ray enters mesh, if viewpoint is outside).
Iterate through the remaining consecutive pairs of entries.
Identify pairs where one entry refers to a front-facing face and the next refers to a back-facing face.
Let $C_{back}$ be the cell owning the back-facing face (occluding PN) and $C_{front}$ be the cell owning the front-facing face (occluded PN).
Add a PN entry containing $C_{front}$ to the `PN_list` of $C_{back}$.
Apply the move-to-front heuristic: if $C_{front}$ is already in $C_{back}$'s `PN_list`, move it to the head.
Set `sink_cell_flag` of $C_{front}$ to `false`.
A cell is a sink cell if its `sink_cell_flag` is `true`.
These cells have no outbound PN or MPVO relations pointing away from them in the dependency graph.
Initialize an empty output list `ordered_cells`.
- MPVO neighbors (from Phase I/standard MPVO relations).
- PN neighbors (cells listed in `c`'s `PN_list`).
If $n$ is not visited, call `RECURSIVE-DFS(n)`.
The `ordered_cells` list contains the cells in reverse topological order (back-to-front).
Reverse this list to obtain the front-to-back rendering order.
- **Overlapping Faces:** If faces overlap but are not sampled at points within the overlap region, the generated sort may not be a strict visibility ordering.
- **Viewpoint Position:** If the viewpoint is outside the mesh, the PIX lists have an even number of entries.
The first entry (exit) and last entry (entry) are discarded.
This is the core modification of Phase II.
It defines occlusion relations based on consecutive front-facing/back-facing face pairs on a PIX list.

The cell contributing the back-facing face is the "occluding PN," and the other is the "occluded PN." This method captures image-space occlusion that may not be represented by explicit mesh topology (MPVO relations).
It is chosen when exact image-space visibility is required for unstructured meshes with complex boundaries or disconnected components.
- **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the scan conversion (Phase I) and the DFS.
The PN extraction iterates through PIX lists.
The move-to-front heuristic ensures that frequently encountered PN relations are found quickly, keeping list traversal efficient.
The DFS is linear in the number of cells and relations.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for PIX lists (proportional to image resolution and mesh complexity) and PN lists (proportional to the number of PN relations).
Provides exact image-space visibility ordering.
Performance depends on the coherence of the scan conversion process.
- **When to use:** Unstructured mesh volume rendering where exact visibility is critical and the mesh is acyclic.
